newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Guardian PMPA to raise motor insurance premiums.
newsitem.headline: Guardian PMPA to raise motor insurance premiums.

text.p: Guardian PMPA Group, Ireland's largest motor insurer, said on Monday that it will increase its motor insurance premiums by an average of five percent with effect from November 1.
The decision to raise premiums is a direct consequence of the increase in road fatalities and injuries this year, Guardian PMPA said in a statement.

The company said police statistics showed that accidents involving death and serious injury rose by almost nine percent in the period to end-August while those involving damage to cars were up by over 12 percent compared with 1995.

"After two years of falling motor insurance premiums, it is regrettable that we have now been forced to raise the premiums charged to our motor insurance policyholders," Gerard Healy, chief executive of Guardian PMPA, said.
He said the deteriorating position in regard to road safety was a worrying trend and called on the government and police to do everything in their power to reduce road accidents.

"Stricter enforcement of road traffic legislation is essential if we are to avoid further increases in the number of deaths and serious injuries on our roads which in turn would trigger off even sharper rises in motor premiums," he said.

Healy said the price increase now being applied was the minimum required to cover the increased cost of claims and further price increases would be inevitable unless action was taken to contain the rising cost of claims.
